segments.text: whom is absorbed in this kind of recitation of Ajapa Gaitri,
for him his daily routine of life is as follows.
Dhanam, Atma Ghanam, his only purpose of his living in his body is just to bestow his knowledge to others.
This is the purpose of his life, remaining period of life.
To bestow his real knowledge of God consciousness to others.
Prokht Chaitanya Rupa Syaathvano Yath Ghanam, the one who has become one with God consciousness, whatever he experiences.
That is whatever he sees in his own self.
That is for him Dhan. Dhan means, there are two meanings of Dhan.
Many meanings.
Diyate Paripurnamsa Rupa, Dhan is that what gives him fullness of his consciousness.
Diyate Kandate Vesubeda, Dhan is that which destroys the differentiated perception of universe for him.
Dhan is that when the illusion is over.
Illusion comes out of illusion.
Diyate Rakshete Laptha Vesubatma Svavascha.
And Dhan is that where this nature of his God consciousness is all-round protected.
This is the meaning of Dhan.
This is what he functions in his remaining period of life.
Next Diyate, next meaning.
Another meaning of Dhan is whatever is given to others, that is Dhan.
It is for his own person.
This meaning of Dhan what has been already explained is for his person only.
Now for others also he explains what is Dhan.
Atma Gyanam Yeva Anena Ante Vasibyo Diyate.
Ante Vasibyo, those who are his devoted disciples, they get Atma Gyan from him, the knowledge of self.
That is said in some dandras.
Darshanath, Parshanathvapi, Vithatath, Bavsagarath, Tariyashanti, Yogindra, Kulajara, Pratishta.
Those heroes of Yogis who are established in Kulajara, Kulajara system, they reveal the reality of God consciousness to others by mere darshan.
mere seeing, looking or mere touch and thus all his disciples cross over on the other side of this samsara.
Some samsara have repeated births and deaths and they get liberated.
